domain_label: Ludhiana Location Choice & Comparative Sourcing Economics — for a small AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic micro-brand selling in California
purpose: A method for deciding whether to source a small, AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic knitwear micro-brand (selling in California/Turlock) from Ludhiana versus the rival domestic clusters (Tirupur, Panipat, Bhilwara) and the offshore alternatives (Bangladesh, Vietnam, China): framing the decision by use case rather than by commodity landed cost, separating the export-economics frame (where Ludhiana loses) from the product-fit + small-batch-iteration + downstream-margin-capture frame (where Ludhiana wins for our case), scoring every candidate on a transparent comparative location-fit formula, producing an explicit go/no-go with named reopen-conditions, and tagging every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim FACT, ESTIMATE, or UNKNOWN so no fabricated figure for any named firm survives.
assumptions: the use case is fixed: a small low-volume AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic (and acrylic-blend) knitwear micro-brand whose retail and margin capture are in California/Turlock, not a price-driven commodity export buyer
all content is sourced from the Ludhiana owner deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md) and the shared SCOPE_GLOSSARY; cluster facts carry the deep-dive's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags unchanged

no per-firm revenue, piece-rate, or off-paper rupee figure is ever stated as fact for a named firm beyond the publicly-disclosed FACTs already in the deep-dive; benchmark magnitudes are labeled ESTIMATE
the off-paper economy is a structural MECHANISM tagged ESTIMATE: discussion/industry-lore, never a named-party accusation, with every rupee magnitude UNKNOWN by design

Ludhiana's defensible edge is woollen/acrylic specialisation + agglomeration small-batch capacity + downstream US margin capture, never landed cost; for cheap high-volume cotton export the rational answer is Tirupur or Bangladesh
the single highest-leverage confirmation for the location verdict is a real Ludhiana per-piece piece-rate plus actual MOQ, yarn price and yarn-to-knit lead times (UNKNOWN here, carried to T2/T4/T9)
exclusions: the make-vs-buy boundary inside Ludhiana (own spinning/knitting vs CMT vs full-package FOB) — covered by the manufacturing-economics KB
the bottom-up Ludhiana cost stack and the compliance-premium magnitude — covered by the manufacturing-economics KB
yarn count/shade/price negotiation and yarn-market mechanics — covered by the yarn/fibre KB
any landed-cost-to-California unit-economics model (freight, duty, drawback, RoSCTL pass-through) — covered by the logistics/unit-economics KB
any claim that a named person or firm pays bribes, evades tax, or is politically captured
source_description: tagged comparative-sourcing facts and labeled benchmark estimates for choosing Ludhiana versus rival Indian clusters and offshore alternatives for a small AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic micro-brand selling in California, grounded in the Ludhiana owner deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md section 6 and bottom line) and the shared SCOPE_GLOSSARY; cluster product-fit and export-disadvantage reads come from the deep-dive, offshore wage/tariff/FTA reads from its offshore table, and the use-case verdict from its bottom line, with every dollar/wage/regulation/behaviour claim carrying its FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag
source_citation: Ludhiana owner deep-dive DEEPDIVE.md (section 6 domestic + offshore alternatives, bottom line, open questions) and SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md; within them: Ludhiana ~90-95% of India's woollen/acrylic knitwear [FACT band]; Tirupur FY24-25 knitwear exports ~Rs40,000 cr / ~US$5B, ~90% of India's cotton-knit exports [FACT]; Panipat recycled/shoddy wool [FACT]; Bhilwara synthetic suiting / >1M synthetic spindles [FACT]; Bangladesh RMG min wage ~US$95-114/month (~25% below India) + EU EBA duty-free graduating 2026 [FACT]; Vietnam wages higher than India, wins on productivity + CPTPP/EU-Vietnam FTAs [FACT]; China highest wages, scale/quality benchmark [FACT]; the awkward-global-middle placement [ESTIMATE, med-high]; apparel duty cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% vs wool 6110.11 ~16% vs acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%, RoSCTL extended to 31 Mar 2026 [FACT, SCOPE_GLOSSARY]; per-piece rate, MOQ, yarn price, lead times [UNKNOWN], carried to T2/T4/T9

competency_questions.question: What is the fixed use case, and why does framing the location choice by use case rather than by commodity landed cost change the answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USE_CASE_FRAME states the small AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic micro-brand selling in California, low-volume and margin-captured downstream, and EXPORT_VS_DOMESTIC_FRAME shows Ludhiana is a domestic-market product cluster not an export-cost cluster, so a price-driven frame and a product-fit frame reach opposite verdicts

competency_questions.question: Why is Tirupur structurally superior for cotton-knit export, and when does that make it the right answer over Ludhiana?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIRUPUR_ALT gives the ~Rs40,000 cr / ~US$5B FY24-25 export figure, ~90% of India's cotton-knit exports, coastal+cotton-belt+mature-export ecosystem [FACT], and states it wins only on a cotton-leaning high-volume export frame, not on woollen/acrylic small-batch

competency_questions.question: What roles do Panipat and Bhilwara actually play, and why is neither a maker for our branded woollen/acrylic sweater?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PANIPAT_ALT is read as a recycled/shoddy-wool feedstock angle only and BHILWARA_ALT as synthetic-suiting/yarn-scale only, each disqualified as a place to make branded sweaters

competency_questions.question: Why does Ludhiana lose on export economics specifically, distinct from losing on product?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LUDHIANA_EXPORT_DISADVANTAGE names landlocked/high-export-freight, Punjab power cost/reliability, high working-capital interest, aging migrant skill base, and seasonal woollen lock-in as the export-cost disadvantages, separate from product-fit

competency_questions.question: What is Bangladesh's edge and its friction for a micro-brand, and why is the duty advantage the wrong market for us?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BANGLADESH_ALT states ~US$95-114/month RMG wage (~25% below India) + EU EBA duty-free (graduating 2026) [FACT], cotton-knit specialised, and flags the duty edge is EU-not-US and the high-MOQ/relationship friction at micro-volume

competency_questions.question: Why are Vietnam and China not cost plays for a micro-brand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VIETNAM_ALT shows wages higher than India, winning on productivity + CPTPP/EU-Vietnam FTAs but over-MOQ for micro, and CHINA_ALT shows the highest-wage scale/quality benchmark, not a cost play and not micro-volume-friendly

competency_questions.question: Where does India/Ludhiana sit globally, and why is that placement fatal for a price-driven export buyer but not for us?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GLOBAL_MIDDLE_PLACEMENT states the awkward-global-middle read (cheaper than Vietnam/China, pricier than Bangladesh, without Bangladesh's tariff preference or Vietnam's FTA web) tagged ESTIMATE med-high, and says it is rarely cost-optimal for a price-driven buyer

competency_questions.question: What is the product-fit reason Ludhiana wins our case despite losing on cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRODUCT_FIT_EDGE ties Ludhiana's ~90-95% national woollen/acrylic specialisation [FACT band] to our exact product and shows no cheaper alternative (Bangladesh cotton-knit, Tirupur cotton, Vietnam/China volume) matches the woollen/acrylic + small-batch + design-iteration combination

competency_questions.question: Why does Ludhiana's agglomeration suit an AI-design brand's small-batch iteration better than a long-run offshore factory?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGGLOMERATION_ITERATION_EDGE explains the walking-distance subcontracting mesh (knit/link/dye/embroider job-work) as built for fast small varied runs, far better than placing tiny experimental orders into a Bangladesh/Vietnam factory tuned for long runs

competency_questions.question: Why does downstream US D2C margin capture mean the factory landed cost is not the whole game?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOWNSTREAM_MARGIN_EDGE shows our margin is captured in California D2C (the same manufacture-to-own-brand logic the cluster's winners proved), so the factory gate should not be over-optimised when the margin is downstream

competency_questions.question: How is a comparative location-fit score computed across the candidates so the verdict is transparent rather than asserted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCATION_FIT_SCORE_FORMULA states the weighted location_fit_score over product_fit, iteration_fit, downstream_margin_fit, export_cost (penalty) and micro_MOQ_fit with a worked recomputable example, and CANDIDATE_SCORECARD applies it to Ludhiana and the rivals with every weight and input labeled

competency_questions.question: How is every money/wage/regulation/behaviour claim in the comparison kept honest so no fabricated or accusatory figure survives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCATION_HONESTY_GUARDRAIL enforces FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging, forbids any named-firm revenue/piece-rate/bribe-as-fact, and holds every off-paper rupee magnitude UNKNOWN as a structural mechanism

competency_questions.question: What is the go/no-go verdict for sourcing our use case from Ludhiana, and what frame would flip it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCATION_GO_NOGO returns GO for Ludhiana on the product + iteration + downstream-margin frame and NO-GO on any cheap-high-volume-cotton-export frame (redirecting to Tirupur/Bangladesh), composing the scorecard, the edges and the honesty guardrail

competency_questions.question: What explicit conditions reopen the location question, and how are the comparative reads refreshed when the underlying figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REOPEN_CONDITIONS names the strategy-flip triggers (priority becomes cost-per-unit at volume, the line goes cotton, volume outgrows micro-MOQ) and LOCATION_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and the data triggers (real piece-rate, MOQ, lead time, tariff/FTA change, EBA graduation) that re-run the scorecard and verdict

glossary.definition: The binding lens for the whole location decision: a small, low-volume, AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic knitwear micro-brand whose retail and margin capture are in California/Turlock; not a price-driven commodity export buyer. Every candidate read is judged against this frame, not against commodity landed cost.

The distinction that Ludhiana is the right product cluster (it owns ~90-95% of India's woollen/acrylic knitwear know-how [FACT band]) but the wrong cost cluster (globally mid-tier, landlocked, no captive-power/scale edge for a small entrant); use it for what it owns, never because it is cheap.

Ludhiana's structural penalties when judged as an export-landed-cost source: landlocked far from any port (high export freight + lead time), Punjab power cost/reliability, high working-capital interest, an aging migrant skill base, and seasonal woollen product lock-in [FACT]; distinct from any product-fit judgement.

India/Ludhiana's placement cheaper than Vietnam/China but pricier than Bangladesh, without Bangladesh's tariff preference or Vietnam's FTA web; rarely cost-optimal for a price-driven export buyer [ESTIMATE, med-high]. It is fatal for a commodity buyer and irrelevant for a product/iteration/margin-driven micro-brand.

The EU 'Everything But Arms' duty-free access Bangladesh enjoys as an LDC (graduating ~2026); the core of Bangladesh's tariff edge, but it is an EU edge, not a US one, so it does not help a brand selling into California [FACT].

The minimum-order-quantity and relationship overhead that long-run-tuned offshore factories (Bangladesh/Vietnam/China) impose, which a tiny experimental capsule order cannot clear economically; the reason offshore cost edges do not reach a micro-brand. Specific MOQs are UNKNOWN, carried to T2.

Ludhiana's dense walking-distance job-work mesh (knit, link, dye, embroider subcontracted within reach) that supports fast, small, varied runs — samples, capsules, frequent design changes — far better than a factory tuned for long runs; the tailwind an AI-design brand actually uses [FACT cluster mechanism].

The principle that our profit is taken in California D2C, not at the factory gate, mirroring the cluster winners' manufacture-to-own-brand-retail move; it means the factory landed cost is not the whole game and the factory gate should not be over-optimised when the margin is downstream.

A transparent weighted composite scoring each candidate on product_fit, iteration_fit, downstream_margin_fit, an export_cost penalty and micro_MOQ_fit; a comparative ranking method, not a claim of measured cost, with every weight and input labeled and the export_cost term entering as a penalty.

An explicit trigger that invalidates the GO verdict and re-opens the location question: the priority becomes cost-per-unit at volume, the line shifts to cotton, or volume outgrows micro-MOQ — in which cases the rational answer becomes Tirupur (cotton export) or Bangladesh (cost + tariff), not Ludhiana.

nodes.definition: Fix the binding frame for the entire location decision: a small, low-volume, AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic (and acrylic-blend) knitwear micro-brand whose retail and margin capture are in California/Turlock, not a price-driven commodity export buyer. This frame is held constant for every candidate read below: the question is never 'who is cheapest landed' but 'who best fits small-batch woollen/acrylic with design iteration and downstream margin'. Misreading the frame as commodity export is the single error that flips the whole verdict to the wrong cluster.

included: the small AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic micro-brand definition
low volume and California/Turlock margin capture

pros.claim: Fixing the use case up front prevents every downstream read drifting into a commodity-cost comparison the brand is not making
pros.example: judging Bangladesh on US$/piece is irrelevant once the frame is small-batch woollen/acrylic with downstream margin

cons.claim: A narrow fixed frame can hide that the frame itself may change as the brand scales
cons.example: if volume grows the micro-brand frame stops holding and the verdict must reopen

failure_modes: judging candidates on commodity landed cost despite the fixed non-commodity frame
treating the frame as permanent rather than re-checkable as volume grows
acceptance_tests: the use case is stated as a small low-volume AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic micro-brand with California/Turlock margin capture and explicitly not a price-driven commodity export buyer, and is named as the frame all candidate reads are judged against
revisit_triggers: the brand's volume outgrows the micro frame
the product line shifts away from woollen/acrylic
the margin-capture point moves out of California D2C

base.update_signal: the use-case frame (volume, product, margin point) changes

nodes.definition: Establish the distinction that decides the whole analysis: Ludhiana is overwhelmingly a domestic-market woollen/acrylic product cluster, not an export-cost cluster, so a price-driven export frame and a product-fit frame reach opposite verdicts. Buying into Ludhiana buys its product know-how and small-batch mesh, NOT export competitiveness — two very different things. The right read is 'right product cluster, wrong cost cluster': use it for what it genuinely owns, never because it is cheap (globally it is mid-tier). This node is the hinge that routes every candidate comparison to the correct frame.

excluded: Ludhiana's specific export-cost penalties (its own node)
the product-fit edge detail (its own node)

pros.claim: Separating the product frame from the cost frame stops a true product cluster being rejected on a cost comparison it was never going to win
pros.example: Ludhiana fails a landed-cost test yet is the only national home of the woollen/acrylic small-batch capability we need

cons.claim: The two-frame split can be abused to excuse any cost disadvantage as 'not the relevant frame'
cons.example: rationalising an uncompetitive landed cost by always invoking product fit even when cost has become the priority

failure_modes: collapsing the two frames and reading Ludhiana as an export-cost play
using the product frame to wave away a cost disadvantage after the priority has flipped to cost
acceptance_tests: Ludhiana is stated as a domestic-market product cluster not an export-cost cluster, the buy-product-know-how-not-export-competitiveness point is made, and the right-product-wrong-cost framing routes which frame governs which question
revisit_triggers: the priority shifts from product to cost-per-unit
Ludhiana's domestic-vs-export orientation changes
a credible current export-output figure replaces the stale pre-2020 numbers

base.update_signal: Ludhiana's domestic-vs-export orientation or the governing priority changes

nodes.definition: Read Tirupur (Tamil Nadu) as the structurally superior location for cotton-knit export that Ludhiana cannot match: FY24-25 knitwear exports ~Rs40,000 cr (~US$5B), ~90% of India's cotton-knit exports, coastal (near ports), in the cotton belt, with a mature export ecosystem [FACT]. The decisive caveat for us: Tirupur is cotton-knit, not woollen/acrylic. If the line ever goes cotton-leaning and high-volume for export, Tirupur deserves a hard look on export logistics alone; for branded woollen/acrylic sweaters it is simply not the product cluster.

included: the ~Rs40,000 cr / ~US$5B export figure and ~90% cotton-knit share
the cotton-not-woollen disqualifier for our product
excluded: the offshore cotton alternatives (their own nodes)

pros.claim: Naming Tirupur's cotton-export superiority keeps the verdict honest about where Ludhiana genuinely loses
pros.example: ~US$5B exports and port proximity make Tirupur the right answer the moment the frame becomes cotton export

cons.claim: Tirupur's strength is product-specific, so citing its export scale can mislead if read as a general superiority over Ludhiana
cons.example: its cotton-knit dominance says nothing about woollen/acrylic small-batch capability

failure_modes: treating Tirupur's cotton-export superiority as a reason to source woollen/acrylic there
ignoring that the Tirupur case only activates on a cotton-leaning high-volume export frame
acceptance_tests: Tirupur is given the ~Rs40,000 cr / ~US$5B FY24-25 figure, ~90% cotton-knit export share, and coastal+cotton-belt+mature-export advantages [FACT], with the cotton-not-woollen disqualifier for our product stated
revisit_triggers: a Tirupur export-figure update
our line shifts cotton-leaning or high-volume-export
a port/logistics change alters Tirupur's export edge

base.update_signal: a Tirupur export figure or our product-frame changes

nodes.definition: Read Panipat (Haryana) for what it actually is: a home-textiles centre and India's hub for recycled/shoddy wool, i.e. low-cost woollen feedstock [FACT]. Its relevance to us is strictly a feedstock angle (a possible source of cheap recycled-wool yarn), not a place to make branded sweaters. It is disqualified as a maker for a premium-leaning AI-designed woollen/acrylic D2C line because its specialisation is recycled-fibre volume, not fashion knitwear construction.

included: Panipat as recycled/shoddy-wool feedstock and home textiles
the disqualification as a branded-sweater maker
excluded: the Bhilwara synthetic comparison (its own node)

pros.claim: Placing Panipat as a feedstock angle prevents it being mistaken for a competing maker location
pros.example: recycled/shoddy wool is an input source, not a fashion-knit production base

cons.claim: Dismissing Panipat as feedstock-only could overlook a genuine low-cost-yarn sourcing option
cons.example: a value acrylic-blend line might still draw on Panipat recycled feedstock

failure_modes: treating Panipat as a branded-sweater maker
ignoring its legitimate role as a recycled-wool feedstock source
acceptance_tests: Panipat is identified as recycled/shoddy-wool feedstock and home textiles [FACT], its relevance limited to a feedstock angle, and it is disqualified as a place to make branded sweaters
revisit_triggers: a recycled-wool feedstock sourcing decision is opened
Panipat's specialisation shifts toward fashion knitwear
a value/recycled line is considered

base.update_signal: a feedstock sourcing decision or Panipat specialisation changes

nodes.definition: Read Bhilwara (Rajasthan) as Asia's largest synthetic textile hub: synthetic suiting and >1 million synthetic spindles [FACT]. It competes on synthetic yarn/fabric scale, not on knitwear, and is not our maker. Its only conceivable relevance is as a synthetic-fibre yarn-scale reference; it has no role in producing a branded, small-batch, design-iterated woollen/acrylic D2C sweater, which is a flat-knit construction problem Bhilwara's suiting base is not built for.

included: Bhilwara as synthetic suiting + >1M synthetic spindles
competition on yarn/fabric scale not knitwear
excluded: the Panipat feedstock comparison (its own node)

pros.claim: Classifying Bhilwara as synthetic-suiting scale prevents confusing yarn-scale with knitwear capability
pros.example: >1M synthetic spindles is a fabric/yarn-scale signal, not a flat-knit sweater capability

cons.claim: Writing Bhilwara off entirely could miss its relevance as a synthetic-fibre supply reference
cons.example: a synthetic-blend line might still reference Bhilwara's synthetic yarn scale

failure_modes: treating Bhilwara's synthetic scale as knitwear-making capacity
overlooking its role as a synthetic-yarn-scale reference
acceptance_tests: Bhilwara is identified as synthetic suiting / >1M synthetic spindles [FACT], framed as yarn/fabric-scale not knitwear, and disqualified as our maker
revisit_triggers: a synthetic-blend yarn sourcing decision is opened
Bhilwara's specialisation shifts toward knitwear
a fully-synthetic line is considered

base.update_signal: a synthetic-yarn sourcing decision or Bhilwara specialisation changes

nodes.definition: Catalog why Ludhiana loses on export economics specifically, distinct from any product judgement: it is landlocked (far from any port, so high export freight + lead time), carries Punjab power cost/reliability exposure, faces high working-capital interest on the seasonal cash cycle, sits on an aging migrant skill base, and is product-locked into seasonal woollens [FACT]. For cotton-knit export Tirupur dominates and for cost Bangladesh undercuts; Ludhiana's genuine, defensible edge is woollen/acrylic specialisation + domestic-market access + vertical-integration speed — explicitly NOT landed cost.

included: landlocked/high-export-freight, power, working-capital, aging-skill, seasonal-lock disadvantages
excluded: the offshore cost comparison (its own nodes)

pros.claim: Listing the export-cost penalties keeps the GO verdict from over-claiming and isolates exactly where Ludhiana is uncompetitive
pros.example: landlocked freight + Punjab power + working-capital drag together explain why an export-cost frame rejects Ludhiana

cons.claim: An export-cost penalty list read alone can wrongly condemn Ludhiana for our product-driven case
cons.example: a reader stopping at the disadvantages would reject Ludhiana before reaching its product fit

failure_modes: reading the export-cost disadvantages as a product disqualification
ignoring that these penalties are real and must be budgeted even when product fit wins
acceptance_tests: the five export-cost penalties (landlocked freight, Punjab power, working-capital interest, aging skill base, seasonal lock-in) are named [FACT] and the defensible-edge-is-not-landed-cost correction is stated
revisit_triggers: a port/logistics change cuts Ludhiana export freight
a Punjab power-tariff/reliability change
a working-capital cost or seasonality shift

base.update_signal: a Ludhiana export-cost penalty (freight, power, working-capital, skill, seasonality) changes

nodes.definition: Read Bangladesh as the cost-and-tariff threat that does not reach us: RMG minimum wage ~US$95-114/month (~25% below India) plus EU EBA duty-free access (graduating ~2026), cotton-knit specialised [FACT]. It wins on pure labour cost + EU tariff — but the duty edge is EU, not US, so it does nothing for a brand selling in California, and at our tiny volume the MOQ and relationship friction of a long-run factory is high. It is the right answer only for a cost-and-tariff frame aimed at the EU at volume, not for our case.

included: EU EBA duty-free graduating ~2026 and its EU-not-US limit
the cotton-knit specialism and high-MOQ micro-friction

pros.claim: Pricing Bangladesh's wage+tariff edge and then showing it is EU-not-US dissolves the strongest cost objection to Ludhiana for our case
pros.example: a ~25% wage gap looks decisive until the EBA edge is shown to apply to the EU, not California

cons.claim: The EU-not-US framing holds only while the brand sells into the US; a future EU channel would revive the edge
cons.example: an EU expansion would make Bangladesh's EBA duty-free advantage live again

failure_modes: treating Bangladesh's EU tariff edge as relevant to a US-selling brand
ignoring that the wage edge is real and would matter at high volume for a cost-driven cotton line
acceptance_tests: Bangladesh is given the ~US$95-114/month wage (~25% below India) and EU EBA duty-free (graduating ~2026) [FACT], with the duty edge flagged EU-not-US and the cotton-knit + high-MOQ micro-friction stated
revisit_triggers: the brand opens an EU channel
Bangladesh's wage or EBA status changes (graduation effects)
our volume rises enough to clear offshore MOQ

base.update_signal: a Bangladesh wage/EBA figure or our sales-region/volume changes

nodes.definition: Read Vietnam as a strong mid/large-volume source that is overkill for a micro-brand: wages are higher than India, and it wins not on cheap labour but on productivity + FTAs (CPTPP, EU-Vietnam) + China+1 capital [FACT]. For our case it is over-MOQ and over-built: its advantages are realised at scale and through tariff webs aimed at markets and volumes we do not have. It is not a cost play for us and not micro-volume-friendly.

included: the productivity + CPTPP/EU-Vietnam FTA + China+1 edge
excluded: the China benchmark comparison (its own node)

pros.claim: Showing Vietnam wins on productivity/FTAs at scale, not cheap labour, removes it as a micro-brand cost option cleanly
pros.example: CPTPP/EU-Vietnam advantages need volume and the right destination markets the micro-brand lacks

cons.claim: The over-MOQ dismissal holds only at micro-volume and would reverse as the brand scales into mid-volume
cons.example: a mid-volume relaunch could make Vietnam's productivity+FTA edge attractive

failure_modes: reading Vietnam as a cheap-labour option when its edge is productivity/FTAs
ignoring that it becomes relevant once volume grows past micro
acceptance_tests: Vietnam is stated as higher-wage-than-India winning on productivity + CPTPP/EU-Vietnam FTAs + China+1 [FACT], and read as over-MOQ/over-built for a micro-brand
revisit_triggers: the brand grows to mid/large volume
a Vietnam FTA or wage change
a destination-market shift toward FTA-covered regions

base.update_signal: a Vietnam wage/FTA figure or our volume changes

nodes.definition: Read China as the scale and quality benchmark, not a cost play: highest wages of the offshore set, but an unmatched integrated machinery/yarn ecosystem and scale make it the quality/volume benchmark the others are measured against [FACT]. For a micro-brand it is neither a cost option (highest wages) nor micro-volume-friendly (built for scale). It anchors the upper bound of what integrated capability looks like, which is useful as a reference but irrelevant as a sourcing choice for our tiny woollen/acrylic capsule runs.

excluded: the Vietnam productivity comparison (its own node)

pros.claim: Framing China as the benchmark not a cost play sets the quality reference without making it a sourcing candidate for micro-volume
pros.example: China's integrated ecosystem defines the quality ceiling but its scale and wages exclude it for a tiny capsule

cons.claim: Using China only as a benchmark understates that some niche Chinese suppliers do take small fashion runs
cons.example: a specialist small-run Chinese knitter could in principle serve a micro-brand despite the general scale read

failure_modes: treating China as a cost option despite its highest wages
ignoring its value as the quality/integration benchmark
acceptance_tests: China is stated as highest-wage but the scale/quality benchmark with an integrated machinery/yarn ecosystem [FACT], and read as neither a cost play nor micro-volume-friendly
revisit_triggers: a China wage or trade-policy change
the brand needs benchmark-grade quality at scale
a niche small-run Chinese supplier is identified

base.update_signal: a China wage/policy figure or our quality/scale need changes

nodes.definition: Synthesize the offshore set into India/Ludhiana's global placement: an awkward global middle — cheaper than Vietnam/China, pricier than Bangladesh, without Bangladesh's tariff preference or Vietnam's FTA web [ESTIMATE, med-high]. For a price-driven export buyer Ludhiana is rarely cost-optimal: it has no labour-cost floor, no LDC duty edge, and no FTA cushion. This placement is fatal for a commodity buyer and irrelevant for a product/iteration/margin-driven micro-brand, which is precisely why the use-case frame, not the cost frame, must govern our verdict.

excluded: the individual country edges (their own nodes)

pros.claim: An explicit global-middle placement stops anyone defending Ludhiana on cost and forces the verdict onto the use-case frame
pros.example: labeling Ludhiana rarely cost-optimal makes clear cost is the wrong axis to win on

cons.claim: The awkward-middle placement is an ESTIMATE, so its precision should not be over-read
cons.example: the exact cost rank shifts with currency, tariffs, and product mix and is not a measured cost ladder

failure_modes: treating the awkward-middle ESTIMATE as a measured cost ranking
using the placement to reject Ludhiana for a product-driven case it is not meant to judge
acceptance_tests: the awkward-global-middle placement is stated (cheaper than Vietnam/China, pricier than Bangladesh, without tariff preference or FTA web) tagged ESTIMATE med-high, and read as rarely cost-optimal for a price-driven buyer but irrelevant to our case
revisit_triggers: a tariff/FTA change moves the relative placement
a currency or wage shift across the set
a credible measured cost-ladder becomes available

base.update_signal: a tariff, FTA, wage, or currency shift moves the relative placement

nodes.definition: Establish the first reason Ludhiana wins our case despite losing on cost: its deep, genuine specialisation is exactly our product — woollen/acrylic sweaters — and it owns ~90-95% of that national capability [FACT band]. None of the cheaper alternatives match the woollen/acrylic + small-batch + design-iteration combination: Bangladesh is cotton-knit, Tirupur is cotton, Vietnam/China are volume. Product fit is the load-bearing reason the use-case frame routes to Ludhiana: we are buying the one place that genuinely makes our exact product well at small scale.

included: product fit as the primary routing reason

pros.claim: Anchoring on woollen/acrylic specialisation gives a product reason no cost comparison can dislodge
pros.example: owning ~90-95% of national woollen/acrylic capability is a capability none of the cheaper rivals hold

nodes.definition: Establish the second reason Ludhiana wins our case: an AI-design brand lives on fast, small, varied runs — samples, capsules, frequent design changes — and the cluster's walking-distance subcontracting mesh (knit, link, dye, embroider job-work within reach) is built for exactly that [FACT cluster mechanism]. This is far better than placing tiny experimental orders into a Bangladesh or Vietnam factory tuned for long runs. Agglomeration is the one cluster moat that is a tailwind for a tiny non-integrated brand: the cluster itself is the flexible infrastructure that lets a micro-brand exist at all.

included: fit for fast small varied runs and design iteration
the contrast with long-run-tuned offshore factories

pros.claim: The job-work mesh turns small-batch iteration from a cost penalty into a structural fit

cons.example: spreading a garment across multiple micro-vendors raises the quality-control coordination burden

treating offshore long-run factories as equally able to absorb tiny experimental orders
acceptance_tests: the walking-distance subcontracting mesh (knit/link/dye/embroider job-work) is stated as built for fast small varied runs [FACT cluster mechanism] and contrasted with a long-run-tuned Bangladesh/Vietnam factory

nodes.definition: Establish the third reason Ludhiana wins our case: we capture margin downstream in California D2C, so the factory landed cost is not the whole game. The cluster's own winners proved the same logic — manufacture then own-brand retail (the move that pivots a maker into downstream margin). Our retail is in California rather than Indian EBOs, but the principle is identical: do not over-optimise the factory gate when the margin is captured downstream. This reframes a mid-tier factory cost as acceptable because it is not where our profit is made.

cons.example: if contribution after CAC is thin, factory landed cost suddenly matters again

failure_modes: assuming downstream margin is secure without testing contribution after CAC
using downstream margin to excuse an uncompetitive factory cost when the downstream margin is in fact thin
acceptance_tests: California D2C downstream margin capture is stated, tied to the cluster winners' manufacture-to-own-brand-retail logic, with the do-not-over-optimise-the-factory-gate principle, and the dependence on a real downstream margin flagged

nodes.definition: Make the comparative location ranking computationally explicit and auditable: location_fit_score = 0.30*product_fit + 0.25*iteration_fit + 0.20*downstream_margin_fit - 0.15*export_cost + 0.10*micro_MOQ_fit, where every input is a 0-1 ESTIMATE judged against the fixed use case and export_cost enters as a penalty (higher cost lowers the score). Worked example for Ludhiana: 0.30*0.95 + 0.25*0.90 + 0.20*0.85 + 0.10*0.85 - 0.15*0.70 = 0.285 + 0.225 + 0.170 + 0.085 - 0.105 = 0.660. The score is a transparent function of labeled use-case-fit ESTIMATEs, never a measured cost, producing a comparative rank not a point cost.

included: the weighted location_fit_score formula with the export_cost penalty term
excluded: the full candidate scorecard table (its own node)

pros.claim: A worked weighted formula makes the comparative ranking auditable and reproducible rather than asserted
pros.example: 0.30*0.95 + 0.25*0.90 + 0.20*0.85 - 0.15*0.70 + 0.10*0.85 = 0.660 lets a reader re-derive Ludhiana's score end to end

cons.claim: The formula's inputs are use-case-fit ESTIMATEs, so the output precision is illusory and weights are a judgement
cons.example: shifting the export_cost weight from 0.15 to 0.25 changes the rank without any new fact

failure_modes: presenting the score as a measured cost or a hard ranking rather than a labeled comparative ESTIMATE
treating the chosen weights as objective rather than use-case judgements
acceptance_tests: the location_fit_score formula is stated with its five terms and the export_cost penalty, the worked Ludhiana example recomputes to 0.660, and the inputs are labeled ESTIMATEs judged against the fixed use case
revisit_triggers: the weighting is re-judged as the use case changes
a candidate's fit input is revised by new data
a real piece-rate/MOQ/lead-time figure firms an input

base.update_signal: a weight or a candidate fit-input in the score changes

Ludhiana wins on product + iteration + micro-MOQ; rivals win only the export_cost term, which the use-case frame down-weights.

the exclusion of Panipat/Bhilwara as non-makers

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every comparative claim: tag every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim FACT (cited public source), ESTIMATE (method + basis + confidence, literal word estimate), or UNKNOWN. Never state as fact that a named person or firm pays bribes, evades tax, or is politically captured; never state a fabricated revenue/earnings/piece-rate figure for a named firm as fact — only publicly-disclosed FACTs or labeled benchmark ESTIMATEs. The off-paper economy is a structural MECHANISM tagged ESTIMATE: discussion/industry-lore, with every rupee magnitude UNKNOWN by design. UNKNOWN is a fine, frequent value (the per-piece rate, MOQ, yarn price and lead times are UNKNOWN here). This guardrail governs how every node above may be expressed.

included: the off-paper-mechanism-with-UNKNOWN-magnitude rule and UNKNOWN as a valid value
excluded: the specific comparative figures (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every comparative figure honest and prevents any accusatory or fabricated claim
pros.example: tagging the awkward-middle placement ESTIMATE and holding off-paper magnitudes UNKNOWN stops any figure being read as a measured fact or an accusation

cons.claim: Heavy tagging and frequent UNKNOWNs can make the comparison read as too hedged to act on
cons.example: a reader wanting a single cheapest-source answer is frustrated by an ESTIMATE-heavy, UNKNOWN-laden comparison

failure_modes: stating a named-firm piece-rate or revenue as fact beyond the disclosed FACTs
asserting any named party engages in bribery, evasion or capture, or quoting an off-paper rupee magnitude as if known
acceptance_tests: every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim is FACT, ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN, no named person/firm is alleged to bribe/evade/be-captured, no fabricated named-firm figure appears, and off-paper magnitudes are held UNKNOWN as a mechanism
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a money/behaviour claim
a disclosed FACT source updates
a previously UNKNOWN figure (piece-rate, MOQ, lead time) becomes available

base.update_signal: a new money/behaviour claim is introduced or an UNKNOWN figure becomes available

nodes.definition: Produce the location verdict for our use case, composing the scorecard, the product/iteration/margin edges, the export disadvantage and the honesty guardrail. The merged rule: GO for Ludhiana on the product + agglomeration small-batch/iteration + downstream US margin-capture frame (where it scores highest and is the only national home of woollen/acrylic small-batch); NO-GO on any cheap-high-volume-cotton-export frame, which redirects to Tirupur (cotton export) or Bangladesh (cost + tariff). Be clear which game is being played before committing: Ludhiana wins our case and loses any commodity-export case. The verdict never claims a cost advantage and budgets the compliance premium as a known line item rather than an edge.

included: the redirect to Tirupur/Bangladesh on a cost frame

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one frame-conditional verdict gives an actionable GO/NO-GO instead of a muddled cost debate
pros.example: the verdict says GO Ludhiana for our woollen/acrylic micro-brand and NO-GO redirecting to Tirupur/Bangladesh the moment the frame becomes cheap cotton export

cons.claim: A frame-conditional verdict can be gamed by mislabeling the frame to force a preferred answer
cons.example: calling a cost-driven order a product play to justify Ludhiana when cost has actually become the priority

failure_modes: issuing GO while quietly relying on a cost advantage Ludhiana does not have
mislabeling a commodity-export frame as a product frame to force a Ludhiana GO
acceptance_tests: the verdict returns GO for Ludhiana on the product + iteration + downstream-margin frame and NO-GO (redirect to Tirupur/Bangladesh) on a cheap-high-volume-cotton-export frame, with no claimed cost advantage and the compliance premium named as a line item
revisit_triggers: a scorecard input or edge feeding the verdict changes
a reopen-condition fires
the governing frame is reclassified

base.update_signal: a scorecard input, edge, or governing frame feeding the verdict changes

nodes.definition: Name the explicit conditions that invalidate the GO verdict and reopen the location question: (1) the priority becomes cost-per-unit at volume; (2) the product line shifts to cotton; (3) volume outgrows micro-MOQ so offshore factories become enterable. In any of these the rational answer stops being Ludhiana and becomes Tirupur (cotton export) or Bangladesh (cost + tariff), or Vietnam/China at larger scale. These are stated up front as binding go/no-go reopen-conditions, not afterthoughts, so a frame change forces a re-decision rather than a quiet drift into the wrong cluster.

included: the cost-at-volume, cotton-shift, and outgrown-micro-MOQ reopen triggers
excluded: the verdict composition itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Stating reopen-conditions up front stops a frame change drifting silently into the wrong cluster
pros.example: a shift to cost-per-unit at volume immediately fires the reopen and routes to Tirupur/Bangladesh

cons.claim: Reopen-conditions are qualitative thresholds, so judging when one has actually fired is a judgement call
cons.example: deciding the volume has truly outgrown micro-MOQ is not a sharp line

failure_modes: letting a fired reopen-condition pass unacted so the verdict goes stale
treating the reopen thresholds as sharp when they are judgement calls
acceptance_tests: the three reopen-conditions (cost-per-unit at volume, cotton shift, outgrown micro-MOQ) are named with their redirect targets (Tirupur/Bangladesh, Vietnam/China at scale) and stated as binding go/no-go reopen-conditions
revisit_triggers: a reopen-condition fires
the priority, product, or volume profile approaches a reopen threshold
a new structurally-superior alternative emerges

base.update_signal: a reopen-condition fires or a frame variable approaches its threshold

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the location verdict current. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major sourcing-data release) plus material-change triggers — a real Ludhiana per-piece piece-rate, actual MOQ, yarn price and yarn-to-knit lead times landing (the UNKNOWNs that firm the scorecard inputs); a US tariff/Section-301-type change or RoSCTL post-2026 continuation; Bangladesh EBA graduation taking effect; a Tirupur/Vietnam/China wage or FTA shift — that route the analysis back through CANDIDATE_SCORECARD and LOCATION_GO_NOGO. Without this loop the verdict silently goes stale as the offshore tariff/wage landscape and the still-missing Ludhiana piece-rate move.

included: the data-trigger list (piece-rate/MOQ/lead-time, tariff/FTA, EBA graduation, rival wage shift)
re-entry into the scorecard and the verdict

pros.claim: A trigger list with the missing-piece-rate confirmation keeps the lowest-confidence scorecard inputs on a path to resolution
pros.example: a real Ludhiana piece-rate landing fires the loop and replaces an ESTIMATE input with a firmer one

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the verdict without new signal, since most inputs (tariffs, wages) update slowly
cons.example: re-scoring monthly when wage and FTA data move yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the verdict ages silently past the tariff/wage landscape
ignoring a fired trigger (the piece-rate landing) and continuing on stale ESTIMATEs
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit data-trigger list exist (piece-rate/MOQ/lead-time, US tariff/RoSCTL, EBA graduation, rival wage/FTA shift), each routing back to CANDIDATE_SCORECARD and LOCATION_GO_NOGO, with the missing Ludhiana piece-rate named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs update
a previously UNKNOWN scorecard input becomes available

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

dominance_rules.rationale: no per-firm piece-rate or off-paper magnitude is known, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named firm's cost or a single cheapest-source answer
dominance_rules.action: answer only with labeled ESTIMATEs plus confidence and a confirmation path, holding piece-rate and off-paper magnitudes UNKNOWN

dominance_rules.rule: Product fit dominates the export-cost penalty within the use-case frame
dominance_rules.rationale: Ludhiana is the only national home of woollen/acrylic small-batch and its edge is never landed cost
dominance_rules.trigger: the export-cost penalty is used to reject Ludhiana for our product case
dominance_rules.action: down-weight export cost, budget it as a known line item, and keep product fit governing unless a reopen-condition flips the frame

dominance_rules.rule: A fired reopen-condition dominates a standing GO verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a frame change to cost-at-volume or cotton invalidates the product-frame verdict
dominance_rules.trigger: the priority, product, or volume crosses a reopen threshold
dominance_rules.action: re-run the verdict and redirect to Tirupur/Bangladesh/Vietnam as the trigger dictates

dominance_rules.rule: Tirupur dominates Ludhiana on a cotton-leaning high-volume export frame
dominance_rules.rationale: Tirupur is the structurally superior cotton-knit export cluster Ludhiana cannot match
dominance_rules.trigger: the line goes cotton and high-volume for export
dominance_rules.action: route the verdict to Tirupur on export logistics

dominance_rules.rule: The EU-not-US qualifier dominates Bangladesh's tariff edge for a US-selling brand
dominance_rules.rationale: the EBA duty-free advantage applies to the EU, not California
dominance_rules.trigger: Bangladesh's EBA edge is applied to US sales
dominance_rules.action: discount the tariff edge unless and until an EU channel exists

dominance_rules.rule: The ESTIMATE label dominates the scorecard's apparent precision
dominance_rules.rationale: the fit inputs and weights are use-case judgements, not measured cost
dominance_rules.trigger: the score is read as a measured cost ranking
dominance_rules.action: present the score as a labeled comparative ESTIMATE with a confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream verdict built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a verdict cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the UNKNOWN piece-rate or an ESTIMATE fit-input carries the verdict above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the verdict's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the use-case frame before reading any candidate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scoring candidates on commodity cost and then re-doing every read once the frame is restored

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every money/regulation/behaviour claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate the export-cost frame from the product frame before judging Ludhiana
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rejecting Ludhiana on cost and then re-deriving the product-fit case from scratch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the location-fit formula and label its inputs before scoring candidates
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scorecard built on unlabeled inputs that must be re-tagged as ESTIMATEs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the EBA edge EU-not-US the first time Bangladesh is scored
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream verdict inheriting an EU tariff advantage wrongly applied to US sales

anti_rework_rules.rule: State the reopen-conditions up front, not after the verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a frame change drifting silently into the wrong cluster before anyone re-decides

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the per-piece rate, MOQ, yarn price and lead times UNKNOWN and name their confirmation path as the scorecard is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to inputs already published as if firm

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make the downstream-margin cushion conditional on contribution after CAC when it is first invoked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a verdict that excuses factory cost on a downstream margin that later proves thin and must be re-judged

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real Ludhiana per-piece piece-rate, actual MOQ, yarn price, or yarn-to-knit lead time lands
iteration_protocol.action: firm the affected scorecard inputs and re-run the verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a US tariff/Section-301-type change or RoSCTL post-2026 continuation is decided
iteration_protocol.action: re-score the candidates on the changed duty/rebate landscape and re-run the verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Bangladesh EU EBA graduation (~2026) takes effect
iteration_protocol.action: re-score Bangladesh and re-read the offshore placement

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reopen-condition fires (priority becomes cost-at-volume, the line shifts to cotton, or volume outgrows micro-MOQ)
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the verdict toward Tirupur/Bangladesh/Vietnam as the trigger dictates

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Tirupur/Vietnam/China wage, FTA, or export-figure update lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-score the affected candidate and re-read the global-middle placement

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Punjab power-tariff or Ludhiana logistics/port change alters the export-cost penalty
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the export disadvantage and re-score the export_cost term for Ludhiana

iteration_protocol.trigger: the California D2C contribution after CAC weakens materially
iteration_protocol.action: re-test the downstream-margin cushion and re-weight the downstream_margin_fit term

iteration_protocol.trigger: a credible current Ludhiana output/export figure replaces the stale pre-2020 numbers
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the export-vs-domestic framing and the placement

priority_rationale: The use-case frame and the product-vs-cost distinction are foundational because every candidate read and the whole verdict are judged against them; the domestic and offshore alternative reads and Ludhiana's export-cost disadvantage establish where Ludhiana loses on cost; the global-middle placement synthesizes the offshore cost landscape; Ludhiana's three edges (product fit, agglomeration iteration, downstream margin) establish where it wins for our case; the location-fit formula and the candidate scorecard make the comparison transparent and rankable; the honesty guardrail governs every dollar/wage/behaviour expression; and the go/no-go verdict, the reopen-conditions and the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a frame-conditional decision and a self-correcting refresh.
